name: MI-02
label: Safe R

key_factors: District's strong Republican lean of about fifteen points
Moolenaar's overwhelming financial advantage ($2.1M raised, $1.2M on hand vs. $182K raised)
Prediction markets price the Republican at roughly 97 percent
No polls or expert ratings indicate a competitive race
model.rationale: The district's fifteen-point Republican lean, Moolenaar's incumbency, and his lopsided fundraising edge all point the same direction, and prediction markets confirm the race is not viewed as competitive. A favorable national environment for Democrats narrows the expected margin only modestly, leaving a comfortable double-digit Republican advantage.
model.watch: Any late-breaking polling showing Ambrose within single digits, or an unexpected scandal involving the incumbent, would be the main catalysts for revising this forecast.
notes: No expert rater lists this race; treated as safe for the party holding the seat.
No usable general-election polls; forecast rests on fundamentals and expert ratings.

overview:
Michigan's 2nd District is a strongly Republican seat covering central and northern Michigan, and Republican John Moolenaar is seeking re-election as the incumbent. The district's partisan lean of roughly fifteen points Republican forms the backbone of the Republican advantage, and a national environment that favors Democrats this cycle trims that edge without coming close to erasing it.

Moolenaar has raised more than two million dollars and holds over 1.2 million on hand, while Democrat Ben Ambrose has raised about 182,000 dollars with roughly 41,000 available. Prediction markets give the Republican about a 97 percent chance of winning, and no public polls or expert ratings flag the race as competitive. The forecast expects Moolenaar to win by a comfortable double-digit margin, with uncertainty reflecting the absence of local polling rather than any sign of a genuine contest.
